Subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry, residency, retention)

Hi Sofia 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery call about data handling and subprocessors for the clinical notes ingestion use case:

- Primary ask: confirm whether Redwood can avoid retaining PII for derived telemetry and what controls exist for request/response logging.
- Data residency: you need EU data residency for patient-identifiable data, but US-based telemetry for non-PII analytics is OK.
- Subprocessors: specifically flagged telemetry vendors (monitoring/analytics), cloud provider regions, and marketplace flows for onboarding third-party connectors.

Next steps I promised:
1) Attach our current subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_20270630.pdf) with vendor roles and locations.
2) Answer whether telemetry logs include PII and what redaction/retention controls are available.
3) Share a short diagram of the marketplace onboarding flow (will follow if useful).

For the immediate questions: our telemetry vendor collects standard service metrics and request metadata. We do not persist customer prompt/response content to telemetry; logs that could contain PII are scoped to ephemeral traces and can be disabled or configured with a retention policy. See details in the attached subprocessor list  the vendor entries include whether they process PII and their region coverage.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270630.pdf

If useful, I can loop in Security (cc'd Rishi) and Legal/Procurement (cc'd Dev) to speed the questionnaire.

Hi Sofia 

Thanks  answers inline below and attached is the completed questionnaire (high-level answers) plus the official subprocessor export. See attached: redwood_subprocessors_20270630.pdf, acme_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx

1) Telemetry and third-party vendors: request/response bodies (i.e., user prompts and model outputs) are NOT sent to our telemetry providers by default. Telemetry vendors receive service metrics, request metadata (timestamps, latency, error codes), and anonymized usage counters. Customers can opt-in to richer traces for debugging, but that requires explicit configuration and consent.

2) PII in logs & redaction: our logging schema marks the following as PII when present: full names, email addresses, SSNs, medical record identifiers (MRNs), and raw patient notes. We provide an ingestion-time redaction pipeline that can remove or hash fields before forwarding to telemetry. You can configure field-level redaction rules and a retention window (log TTL).

3) Data residency / deployment: we support EU-only Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) that ensure customer data remains in EU regions and a separate control plane option for sensitive customers. I have cc'd Rishi (Security) and Dev (Procurement) to confirm contract language and implementation details for an EU-only commitment.

Notes: the attached subprocessor list shows which vendors process metadata vs content and their region coverage. The telemetry vendor listed (Segment) is noted as processing metadata only; their processing locations include US and EU  we can arrange an EU-only data flow for your EU data if you choose Dedicated/Private.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi to confirm SOC 2 scope and any additional audit artifacts you need.
- Dev to kick off procurement + marketplace/onboarding questions (if you prefer to sign via cloud marketplace).
- I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up with you next week to walk through the redaction config and subprocessor controls.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270630.pdf, acme_security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx

Quick follow-up: marketplace + telemetry notes:

- Marketplace provisioning: Both GCP Marketplace and Azure Marketplace support region constraints at provisioning time for dedicated/private offers; we can route EU customers to EU-only infra when they purchase through the marketplace. There is an implementation checklist (I can drop a link) but it's supported.
- Telemetry via marketplace: telemetry vendor contracts we offer by default are the same; Segment (metadata-only) is the common vendor. No additional subprocessors are injected by marketplace flows, but customers who enable richer tracing for debugging may choose to forward traces to their own Splunk/Datadog  that is an opt-in configuration.
- I'll attach the vendor attestation pack and the marketplace implementation checklist to the HubSpot record now.
